_comment: Tool directory entries. Editable by non-engineers. `universityProvided: true` marks tools provided/endorsed by U-M. Any tool with universityProvided:false MUST render the non-University warning wherever it appears. `approvalStatusNote` is intentionally soft-coded because university-approved status can change — keep it current. DRAFT placeholder content: confirm all details against current U-M/ITS guidance before relying on it.

tools.name: U-M GPT
tools.label: University-provided
tools.shortDescription: U-M's secure, general-purpose generative AI chat built on leading foundation models, with university data protections.
approvedFor: Drafting and editing non-sensitive text
Brainstorming and summarizing
Explaining concepts and general Q&A
tools.dataSensitivityNote: Offers stronger data protections than public consumer chatbots. Confirm current data-handling guidance in ITS documentation before entering any sensitive, regulated, or confidential information.
strengths: Free for U-M staff and students
University data protections vs. public tools
General-purpose and easy to access with U-M credentials
limitations: Not a substitute for authoritative sources; can still hallucinate
Approved data-sensitivity level should be confirmed for regulated data
Not specialized for any single domain
tools.bestFor: Everyday drafting, summarizing, and general questions where no confidential data is involved.
tools.accessPath: Sign in with your U-M credentials at the U-M GPT service (see ITS AI services page for the current URL).

tools.name: U-M Maizey
tools.label: University-provided
tools.shortDescription: U-M's tool for building custom AI assistants grounded in your own documents and data sources (retrieval-augmented).
approvedFor: Answering questions over a defined set of your own documents
Building a project- or team-specific assistant
Summarizing and searching curated internal content
tools.dataSensitivityNote: Because Maizey can be pointed at your own data sources, be especially deliberate about what you upload. Confirm the data classification allowed for your project in current ITS guidance.
strengths: Grounds answers in your provided sources (reduces hallucination)
limitations: Quality depends on the quality/scope of the sources you provide
Setup effort to curate and maintain the knowledge base
Still requires verification of outputs
tools.bestFor: Question-answering and summarization grounded in a specific, curated set of documents you control.
tools.accessPath: Access Maizey with your U-M credentials via the ITS AI services page; create a project and add your data sources.

tools.name: Gemini
tools.label: University-provided
tools.shortDescription: Google's generative AI, available to U-M under the Google Workspace agreement. Approval scope can change — confirm current status.
approvedFor: Drafting and summarizing within approved Google Workspace contexts
General assistance integrated with Google tools
tools.dataSensitivityNote: Availability and approved data classifications depend on the current U-M Google Workspace agreement. Do not assume a data level — confirm current approval status in the Tool Directory / ITS guidance before use.
strengths: Integrated with Google Workspace apps many staff already use
Covered under an existing university agreement
limitations: Approval scope and data-handling terms can change over time
Confirm current U-M approval status before relying on it
General-purpose; verify outputs
tools.bestFor: General drafting and assistance for staff already working inside Google Workspace, once current approval status is confirmed.
tools.accessPath: Available through U-M Google Workspace where enabled; confirm current access and approval status with ITS.

tools.name: ChatGPT (OpenAI)
tools.label: External tool
tools.shortDescription: OpenAI's widely used generative AI chat assistant, available as a free consumer product or paid business/enterprise tiers.
approvedFor: Personal brainstorming on clearly non-confidential topics
Drafting general, publicly-shareable text
Learning/explaining general concepts
tools.dataSensitivityNote: Not University-provisioned. A personal/consumer account's data-use terms differ from an enterprise agreement. Never enter confidential, regulated, or personal data — use a University-approved tool for anything work-related and sensitive.
strengths: Very widely used and familiar to most staff
limitations: Not vetted or licensed by the University for ERM work
Consumer-tier accounts may use inputs for model training unless explicitly opted out
Can hallucinate confidently; always verify outputs
tools.bestFor: Personal, non-work brainstorming or drafting where nothing confidential or University-related is involved.
tools.accessPath: Not a University-provisioned account. If a business use case genuinely requires it, confirm with ITS whether an approved enterprise agreement exists before using it for any ERM work.

tools.name: Claude (Anthropic)
tools.label: External tool
tools.shortDescription: Anthropic's generative AI assistant, known for longer context windows and document-heavy work.
approvedFor: Drafting and reviewing long, non-confidential documents
General research and brainstorming
Explaining or summarizing public materials
tools.dataSensitivityNote: Not University-provisioned. Treat any input as potentially retained by the vendor under consumer terms. Do not paste confidential, regulated, or personal data.
strengths: Strong general reasoning and writing quality
limitations: Not vetted or licensed by the University for ERM work
Consumer-tier data-use terms differ from an enterprise agreement
Still requires human verification of outputs
tools.bestFor: Drafting or summarizing long, non-confidential documents when no University-provided tool is a better fit.
tools.accessPath: Not a University-provisioned account. Confirm with ITS whether an approved enterprise agreement exists before using it for any ERM work.

tools.name: Perplexity
tools.label: External tool
tools.shortDescription: AI-powered search engine that answers questions with inline citations to web sources.
approvedFor: Early-stage research on public, non-confidential topics
Finding a starting set of sources to verify independently
tools.dataSensitivityNote: Not University-provisioned. Search queries are sent to a third-party service — never include confidential or regulated details in a query.
strengths: Good starting point for public-information research
limitations: Cited sources still require independent verification
Not vetted or licensed by the University
Coverage and accuracy vary by topic
tools.bestFor: Quick, citation-backed exploration of a public topic as a starting point — verify every source before relying on it.
tools.accessPath: Publicly available at perplexity.ai. No University license; use only the free tier for non-confidential, public research.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.label: External tool
tools.shortDescription: AI pair-programmer that suggests code completions and explanations inside a code editor.
approvedFor: Drafting boilerplate code and test scaffolding
Explaining unfamiliar code
Speeding up routine scripting tasks
tools.dataSensitivityNote: Not University-provisioned. Do not point it at proprietary, confidential, or regulated code or data unless a business-tier license and data-handling terms have been separately confirmed.
strengths: Strong at boilerplate and common patterns
limitations: Not reviewed or licensed by the University for ERM work
Can suggest insecure or incorrect code — always review before running
Consumer/individual tier data-use terms may differ from business tier
tools.bestFor: Individual coding or scripting tasks (e.g., a small data-processing script) where no confidential data is involved and all code is reviewed before use.
tools.accessPath: Not provisioned by U-M for this purpose. If you already have a personal or team license, confirm with ITS/security whether it's appropriate for ERM-related work first.

tools.name: Otter.ai
tools.label: External tool
tools.shortDescription: AI meeting transcription and summarization tool that joins calls or transcribes recordings.
approvedFor: Transcribing and summarizing meetings with no confidential content
Generating a rough draft of meeting notes for later editing
tools.dataSensitivityNote: Not University-provisioned. Meeting audio/text is processed on vendor servers. Requires informed consent from all participants, and must never be used for meetings touching confidential, regulated, or personal data.
limitations: Not vetted or licensed by the University
Raises consent and data-retention questions for every recorded meeting
Summaries still need human review for accuracy
tools.bestFor: Transcribing routine, non-confidential meetings where every participant has explicitly consented to being recorded.
tools.accessPath: Not University-provisioned. Confirm recording-consent requirements and vendor data-retention terms before use; never use for meetings involving confidential or regulated information.

tools.name: NotebookLM (Google)
tools.label: External tool
tools.shortDescription: Google's AI research assistant that answers questions and summarizes strictly from documents you upload.
approvedFor: Summarizing or querying a small set of your own non-confidential documents
Building a quick study guide or FAQ from source material you provide
tools.dataSensitivityNote: A separate product from core Google Workspace apps — do not assume it falls under U-M's Workspace agreement. Confirm coverage with ITS before uploading any University documents; treat as external until confirmed.
strengths: Grounds answers in the sources you upload (reduces hallucination)
Good for quickly orienting to a new document set
limitations: Coverage under U-M's Google agreement is unconfirmed
Uploaded documents leave your direct control once submitted
Not vetted or licensed by the University for ERM work
tools.bestFor: Summarizing or querying a small set of your own non-confidential documents, once you've confirmed whether it's covered under U-M's Google agreement.
tools.accessPath: Confirm with ITS whether NotebookLM is covered under U-M's Google Workspace agreement before uploading any University documents. If unconfirmed, treat it as an external tool and use only public/non-confidential material.

tools.name: Grammarly
tools.label: External tool
tools.shortDescription: AI-assisted grammar, style, and tone-editing tool available as a browser extension and app integrations.
approvedFor: Grammar and style editing of non-confidential drafts
Tone-checking before sending routine communications
tools.dataSensitivityNote: Runs as a browser extension that can read text on pages you visit, including web-based email and document tools. Do not enable it on pages containing confidential, regulated, or personal information unless a University enterprise license is confirmed.
strengths: Lightweight, works across many apps via the browser extension
Catches grammar and tone issues quickly
limitations: University enterprise licensing is unconfirmed — treat as external until verified
Free tier sends page text to Grammarly's servers
Not a substitute for careful proofreading
tools.bestFor: Light grammar and tone editing of non-confidential drafts; confirm with ITS whether a University enterprise license exists before broader use.
tools.accessPath: Confirm with ITS whether U-M has an enterprise Grammarly license. Absent that confirmation, treat it as an external consumer tool and disable it on any page with sensitive content.

tools.name: DeepL
tools.label: External tool
tools.shortDescription: AI-powered translation tool known for high-quality, natural-sounding translations.
approvedFor: Translating short, non-confidential text passages
Getting a quick draft translation to have reviewed by a fluent speaker
tools.dataSensitivityNote: Not University-provisioned. The free tier may store and use submitted text. Never upload full documents containing confidential, regulated, or personal information.
strengths: High translation quality across many languages
Free tier available for casual use
limitations: Not vetted or licensed by the University
Free tier's data-retention terms are less protective than an enterprise agreement
Machine translation still needs review by a fluent speaker for anything official
tools.bestFor: Translating short, non-confidential passages as a starting draft; use a no-data-retention tier and avoid uploading full confidential documents.
tools.accessPath: Publicly available at deepl.com. No University license confirmed — use only for non-confidential text and prefer a paid tier with a no-data-retention policy where possible.
